title: Recombinant DNA and transgenic organisms

draft.title: Recombinant DNA and transgenic organisms
card: Recombinant DNA is DNA made by joining pieces from different sources. A gene is cut from one organism and combined with the DNA of another.
Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sequences. A vector, such as a plasmid (a small ring of DNA in bacteria), carries the gene into the host cell. DNA ligase joins the gene into the vector.
An organism that has received a gene from another species is transgenic. Its cells read the new gene and make the protein it codes for.
Human insulin is made this way. The human insulin gene is placed in bacteria, which then make insulin as they grow and divide.
draft.remember: Cut a gene out, join it into a vector, and the host becomes transgenic.

a.q: Which description fits a transgenic organism?
opts: A bacterium that carries a gene from a human
A sheep that is a genetic copy of its parent
A crop bred from its two highest yielding parents
A plant grown from a cutting of its parent
a.why: A transgenic organism has a gene from another species inserted into its DNA. Selective breeding of crops only mixes genes within one species, so it does not make a transgenic organism.
a.clue: Look for a gene that has moved between species.

b.q: A scientist wants bacteria to make a human protein. She cuts the human gene out and joins it into a plasmid. Which pair of enzymes does she need for these two steps?
opts: Restriction enzyme to cut, DNA ligase to join
DNA ligase to cut, restriction enzyme to join
Restriction enzyme to cut, and to join
DNA ligase to cut, and to join
b.why: A restriction enzyme cuts DNA at a specific sequence, and DNA ligase joins pieces together. Swapping the two is the tempting mistake, because both enzymes act on DNA and their names are easy to mix up.
b.clue: One enzyme cuts at set sequences and the other seals the pieces.

a.best: A bacterium that carries a gene from a human

b.best: Restriction enzyme to cut, DNA ligase to join
